title: API fallback experiments — oncall lab notes and draft runbook
summary: Working draft of quick triage + experiment playbook for common API failure modes: request timeouts, 429 rate responses, degraded streaming, and sudden elevated error rates. Contains immediate responder steps, short-term mitigations, and a small set of lab experiments to validate fallback and routing behavior before production rollouts.
body:
Context:
- Motivation: Oncall frequently faces the same repetitive choices when customers see timeouts/429s/degraded streaming. We need a short, executable checklist responders can follow and a lightweight set of lab experiments to validate our fallback flows (model routing, partial responses, rate-based routing).
- This doc is explicitly intentionally terse — keep it to single-screen actions for first responder + a longer 'lab' section for followups.

Detection signals (quick reference):
- Latency spike: 95p token latency > 2× baseline for > 5m OR 50p request latency > 1s above SLO.
- 429 surge: 5m rolling rate of 429s > 0.5% of requests OR sudden increase from <0.05% to >0.3% in <10m.
- Streaming degradation: client-observed stream stalls (keepalive drops) + increase in partial-response rates. Grafana: streaming-response-duration bucket shift + increase in stream-reset counts.
- Elevated error rate: 5m error rate (5xx) > 0.5% and sustained for 10m.

Primary goals for first 15 minutes:
1) Stabilize customer surface area (reduce blast radius).
2) Keep high-priority traffic alive (canary / enterprise customers).
3) Gather telemetry and attach correlating ids for postmortem.

First-responder checklist (0–15m):
- Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty, add incident channel, ping SRE lead.
- Quick assessment: Are all regions affected? Check global health page and region breakdown.
- Set incident severity (sev3 if limited, sev2/sev1 if major customer impact).
- Collect IDs: pick 3 failing request ids from logs (trace id, request id). Post to incident channel.
- Short-term mitigations (pick as applicable):
  * If 429s: enable emergency rate-shaping for public tier (toggle: service-rate-limit.override=enterprise-only) OR increase token bucket for reserved capacity for 10m.
  * If timeouts: reduce max_seq_length on hot route via config flag (route.max_seq_len=1024) OR temporarily switch route to smaller base model variant.
  * If streaming degraded: switch to non-streaming (polling) fallback for affected endpoints OR enable smaller chunk size (stream.chunk_ms=50->30) to force more frequent keepalives.
  * If error-rate spike: automatically rollback last deploys that touched serving runtime or routing config (use deploy rollback playbook).
- Implement soft-fallback routing: route 5–10% traffic to 'fallback-mini' model variant to relieve pressure and monitor error/latency improvements.
- Start a short lived smoke test: run 10 synthetic requests across region variants and paste results.

Quick commands (examples):
- Check request rates by region: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS' https://internal-metrics/requests?group=region | jq .
- Toggle fallback routing: redwoodctl route update --route-id r_ABC123 --fallback-model fallback-mini --pct 10
- Rollback last runtime deploy: redwoodctl deploy rollback --service serving-runtime --to previous
- Streaming health check (k8s): kubectl -n infra logs deploy/stream-proxy -c proxy --since=10m | tail -n 200

Mitigations per failure mode (short + medium term):
- Timeouts:
  Short: decrease per-request CPU/GPU work by routing to smaller variant; reduce sequence length; increase worker count for the route; enable 'synchronous-kv-cache' for hot prefixes.
  Medium: adjust kernel allocation for long-tail requests; schedule a capacity increase on the dedicated pool; add a circuit-breaker that rejects >X concurrent requests with 503 + Retry-After to offload tail latency.
  Notes: communicate to product if quality vs latency tradeoffs are changed.

- 429s (rate-limited throttles):
  Short: relax global throttle for logged-in tokens only; bump burst window for reserved capacity customers; identify client misbehaving patterns and contact the app owner.
  Medium: tune rate-limiter to be token-aware (dedupe tokens) and increase token-bucket refill for busy times; add routing policy to shift best-effort traffic to low-cost endpoints.
  Long: implement per-customer token pooling and backpressure channels (webhook for client to slow down).

- Degraded streaming:
  Short: fallback to chunked polling; reduce chunk size to increase keepalive frequency; temporarily disable expensive server-side transforms that run in stream pipeline.
  Medium: instrument and increase websocket proxy capacity; fix backpressure handling in stream proxy; set up streaming-specific SLA dashboards.
  Notes: capture one raw websocket session for full binary trace when possible.

- Elevated error rates (5xx):
  Short: identify top failing stack (model server, proxy, infra). If model server: fallback variant; if proxy: recycle pod; if infra (GPU OOM): evict and move workloads.
  Medium: add per-route canary isolation; push hotfix for observed exception.

Experiment lab (for SRE rotation to run within 48–72h after incident):
- Goal: validate that fallback routing + reduced-seq-length + streaming chunk-size changes reduce user-visible errors without unacceptable quality regression.
- Matrix: run combinations of these toggles in staging and canary for 3h each:
  1) route fallback 10%/20%/50% -> measure error/latency
  2) seq_len clamp 4096/2048/1024 -> measure token cost and latency
  3) streaming chunk_ms 80/50/30 -> measure stream stalls and partial responses
- Acceptance criteria: at 10% fallback, 95p token latency drops >=15% and streaming stall rate drops >=30% with <5% degradation in semantic QA baseline (run short eval prompts).
- Test plan steps:
  1) Deploy toggles to staging: redwoodctl route update ...
  2) Run synthetic traffic 100 rps using locust script: tools/locust/streaming-smoke.py
  3) Capture traces and evaluate with evaluation harness: python tools/eval/compare_quality.py --baseline baseline.json --candidate candidate.json
  4) Roll changes to 1% canary in prod for 30m. If metrics improve, upscale.

Post-incident follow-ups and ownership:
- Owner for follow-up experiments: Luis Romero (eng-sre).
- Remediation ticket for infra fixes: JIRA-RI-1243 (already linked).
- Postmortem author: whoever was primary responder — assigned within 48h. Postmortem must include root cause hypothesis, timeline, and recommended configuration changes.

Open questions / TODOs (short list):
- Should we expose a first-class "graceful degrade" API that returns partial_text + estimated_full_time? (product input needed).
- Can we add better guardrails for streaming proxies to preemptively shed load before downstream model queues fill?
- Add unit and integration tests for fallback-mini model so we can validate quality automatically.

Notes to future oncall:
- If you toggle anything, leave a short note in the incident channel with exact command and reason. Don't exceed 30% fallback without approvals.
- If you need to reroute enterprise traffic, double-check billing and quotas — reserved capacity is charged differently.
- Use the synthetic harness for a quick smoke before and after any change. It's under tools/locust and can be run from your laptop with VPN.

Appendix: quick Grafana queries (copy-paste):
- 95p token latency by route: sumSeries(aliasByNode(request_latency_ms.p95.* , 3))
- 429 rate: divideSeries(nonNegativeDerivative(requests.429.count, 60), nonNegativeDerivative(requests.total.count, 60))
- Streaming stalls: increase(stream.proxy.stalls.count, 5m)

End of draft. Add improvements to this doc as you find repetitive steps during oncall rotation.

Changelog:
- 2024-11-05 Nora: initial draft (lab + checklist).
- 2024-12-10 Mei: added streaming chunk experiments.
- 2025-03-21 Owen: clarified quick toggle commands and added acceptance criteria for lab.
